tasks.title: interactions: zone-rule classifier v0 over frame JSONL
tasks.goal: Turn ObservationFrame JSONL into InteractionEvent JSONL with hand-tuned zone rules and event segmentation. This is the always-available classifier everything else falls back to (invariant 7).
acceptance: `uv run --package interactions python -m interactions.run --frames <frames.jsonl> --zones <zones.json> --out events.jsonl` works end to end

Rules: tool inside a bin_slot with overlap and dwell near a wrist gives transfer.scoop (direction bin to tool). Sustained overlap of a hand or tool with a plate or bin gives transfer.contact (both). Sustained moving overlap across a plate gives transfer.wipe (both). Dwell in the wash zone gives clean.wash as a self-loop (a_id == b_id)
The segmenter merges per-frame hits into events with t_start_ms <= t_end_ms and deterministic event_ids. Events come out in t_start_ms order per pair (`safety` test)
Every expected event in the interactions-02 fixtures is matched within a 200 ms tolerance, and the near-miss fixture yields no event with probability >= 0.5: `pytest -k rules_fixtures`
clean.wash needs the wash zone, a minimum dwell and probability >= the configured wash floor. A `safety` test shows a brief pass through the wash zone yields no wash
Every output line validates against interaction_event, with classifier {name: zone_rules, version}
All rule constants live in one config object, logged at startup and encoded in classifier.version

tasks.title: interactions: hand-written frame fixtures with expected events
tasks.goal: Unblock rule development before perception-01 lands, with tiny, readable frame JSONL scenes whose correct events are known.
acceptance: At least 4 fixtures under `components/interactions/tests/fixtures/frames/`: knife scoop from a bin slot, hand touching a plate, tool dwelling in the wash zone, and a near miss (tool passes over a plate without dwell)

Each fixture has 30 frames or fewer, validates against observation_frame, and has a sibling `<name>.expected.json` listing the expected events (action, pair, direction, approximate t_start_ms and t_end_ms)
A matching zones.json fixture with bin_slot, plating_spot and wash zones
`uv run --package interactions pytest components/interactions -k fixtures_valid` passes

tasks.title: interactions: candidate pairs and allergen-blind features
tasks.goal: Generate candidate pairs (hand-tool, tool-bin, tool-plate, hand-bin, hand-plate) and compute InteractionFeatures per pair per frame, with no path for allergen information to leak in (invariant 6).
acceptance: Only the five pair types are generated, and only within a configurable distance or overlap. Unit tests cover each pair type and the cutoff

Features use normalized distance, overlap as intersection over the smaller box, inside_zone, zone_kind (never the zone ID), speeds in normalized units per second, dwell_ms, and wrist_proximity or null
Every feature row validates against interaction_features (additionalProperties false): `pytest -k features_contract`
`safety` import-lint test: the features and classifier modules never import or read bin_profile, entity_risk, allergen units or StateClient reads
`safety` property test: features are identical whatever the bin allergen profiles are
Features are stable across 15, 30 and 60 FPS resamplings of the same scene, within tolerance

tasks.title: interactions: ADR on edge direction and wash self-loop (OQ-9)
tasks.goal: Settle with provenance which way allergens move on each action, and how a wash event (which has no partner entity) is represented.
acceptance: An ADR PR in docs/adr/ covers contact and wipe as both, scoop as source to tool, and wash as a self-loop with a_id == b_id and direction ignored, with the alternatives considered
The provenance Manager posts ACK on the issue
A `type:rfc` issue is filed to document the wash self-loop convention in the interaction_event schema description
OQ-9 is marked for the Director to move to Resolved once merged

tasks.title: interactions: publish recorded event JSONL fixture pack
tasks.goal: Ship the fake that provenance and the e2e harness test against: event JSONL produced by the real zone-rule classifier on known scenes.
acceptance: At least 4 event fixtures under `components/interactions/tests/fixtures/events/`, generated by `interactions.run` from the interactions-02 frames, with the regeneration command in the README
Every line validates against interaction_event
A test regenerates them and fails on drift: `pytest -k event_pack_fresh`
Announced on the provenance Team board with paths

tasks.title: interactions: FallbackClassifier that always lands on zone rules
tasks.goal: Wrap any primary classifier (the LSTM later) so that load failure, exceptions or timeouts fall back to zone rules, and each event names the classifier that produced it (invariant 7).
acceptance: Both zone_rules and FallbackClassifier implement the InteractionClassifier Protocol
`safety` tests: a primary that is missing, raises, or exceeds the timeout yields zone_rules output, with classifier.name = zone_rules on the event
A healthy primary's events carry its own name and version
Fallbacks are logged and counted, and the count is exposed for health reporting
`uv run --package interactions pytest components/interactions -m safety` passes
out_of_scope: Choosing which classifier is primary (adoption ADR, M3)

tasks.title: interactions: streaming pipeline writing edges via StateClient
tasks.goal: Consume ObservationFrames in-process, emit events incrementally and write them through StateClient.record_interactions within 500 ms of event end, never dropping one silently.
acceptance: The pipeline accepts a frame iterator (in-process on the Pi, or JSONL replay) and emits events as segments close
Event end to record_interactions within 500 ms, measured with FakeClock in a test
Batched writes with deterministic, idempotent event_ids. Replaying the same frames twice writes no duplicates
`safety` test: on StateUnavailable, events are buffered and retried, and none are lost once the fake recovers. Buffer depth is exposed for health
Fake-swap test runs frame fixtures through the pipeline into InMemoryStateClient, and its interactions match the event pack: `pytest -k pipeline_e2e`
out_of_scope: Real SpacetimeDB integration on the Pi (M2)

tasks.title: interactions: tune rules on perception's recorded frame pack
tasks.goal: Move from hand-written frames to perception's recorded fixture pack (published after perception-01), label the expected events, and lock them in as a regression suite.
acceptance: Expected-event files for each scene in perception's fixture pack, committed under our tests/fixtures/
Rules re-tuned, with constants changed only in the config object. The PR shows matches and misses before and after
Regression test `pytest -k recorded_pack` passes. No expected transfer is missed, and no false clean.wash occurs
The scene where a tool leaves and re-enters produces events on the new entity ID, never the old one

tasks.title: interactions: labeled clip dataset format and validator
tasks.goal: Define how real recordings and their labels are stored and split, so the owner can start recording (OQ-12) and the benchmark can't leak.
acceptance: Team ADR in docs/adr/: session layout (perception recorder manifest, frames.jsonl, labels.jsonl with pair, action, direction, t_start_ms, t_end_ms, labeler), and a split policy by session, never by clip
`uv run --package interactions python -m interactions.dataset.validate <dir>` checks the layout, label validity against frames, and overlaps
A held-out manifest format with a content hash, so the held-out set can be frozen
A tiny labeled sample session committed under tests/fixtures/ (100 KB or less) passes validation
An owner-facing recording guide posted on the issue (what to film, how long, naming)

tasks.title: interactions: labeling tool v0 for candidate segments
tasks.goal: Let a person label actions quickly by stepping through candidate-pair segments from a recorded session, writing labels.jsonl in the dataset format.
acceptance: `python -m interactions.labeling --session <dir>` steps through candidate segments, takes one keypress per action (contact, scoop, wipe, wash, unimportant, skip), and writes labels.jsonl
Shows the video frame with both boxes when video is available, and falls back to a text view otherwise
Output passes the interactions-09 validator: `pytest -k labeling_output`
Resumable: re-running skips already-labeled segments

tasks.title: interactions: benchmark harness with cost-weighted score
tasks.goal: A frozen, reproducible way to compare classifiers on held-out labeled sessions. It decides LSTM adoption in M3 (invariant 7).
acceptance: `python -m interactions.training.benchmark --classifier zone_rules --heldout <manifest>` writes report.json plus report.md
Event-level matching with temporal IoU, and per-action precision and recall
A cost-weighted score where a missed transfer and a false clean.wash carry the heaviest weights. The weights are documented in the team ADR
Refuses to run if the held-out manifest hash doesn't match the frozen one
Runs on the sample session in CI: `pytest -k benchmark_smoke`

tasks.title: interactions: export per-pair feature windows to JSONL
tasks.goal: Produce the LSTM's training input: time-ordered windows of InteractionFeatures per pair, in a format sim can also generate synthetically.
acceptance: `python -m interactions.training.export_windows --frames <jsonl> --out windows.jsonl --len <n> --stride <k>` writes one window per line
Every row in every window validates against interaction_features. A window never mixes pairs
Window spec (length, stride, padding) documented in the README and shared on the sim Team board
`pytest -k windows` covers boundaries and short tracks
